_design: Food classes by texture/consistency. Cuisine is an array — a dish can belong to multiple state-level food cultures. Swaps are food-class-locked. fills_slots for one-pots. pairs_with is suggestion-layer only. See D-17, D-18, D-19 in decisions-log.md.

cuisine_vocabulary._note: State/cultural level only. No north_indian or south_indian — those are regions, not food cultures. A dish can belong to multiple cuisines.

one_pot.description: Complete meal in one vessel — fills 2+ slots simultaneously. Swaps only with other one_pot dishes covering the same slots via fills_slots superset rule.

grain_staple.description: Dry starchy base — roti, rice, paratha, flatbreads, South Indian tiffin

liquid.description: Thin to medium consistency, spoonable — dal varieties, sambhar, kadhi, rajma, chole, rasam, salan, amti

curry.description: Thick gravy — chicken curry, fish curry, paneer masala, egg curry. Same display as liquid; separate swap pool.

dry_semi_dry.description: No gravy or minimal — pan-fried proteins, bhujia, stir-fry sabzis, poriyal, thoran, kootu

greens.description: Leafy, raw, or lightly cooked — saag, salad, sprouts, kachumber, sarson

side_condiment.description: Accompaniment, never a main slot — curd, raita, chutney, pickle, chaas

snack_finger_food.description: Standalone, no grain needed — tikka, omelette, vada, chilla, dhokla, pesarattu

tag_vocabulary._note: Standardised tags. Only use tags from this list.

items.name: Curd Rice (Thayir Sadam)
items._one_pot_note: Rice mixed with curd. Fills grain and side slots. South Indian comfort staple.

items.name: Khichdi
items._one_pot_note: Rice + dal cooked together. Fills both grain and liquid slots.

items.name: Pongal (Ven Pongal)
items._one_pot_note: Rice + moong dal cooked together South Indian style with pepper and ghee. Fills grain and liquid slots.

items.name: Bisi Bele Bath
items._one_pot_note: Karnataka one-pot: rice + toor dal + vegetables + spice powder cooked together. Fills grain, liquid, and dry slots simultaneously.

items.name: Chicken Biryani
items._one_pot_note: Spiced rice + chicken cooked together. Fills grain and protein slots. Traditionally paired with salan and raita.

items.name: Dal Dhokli
items._one_pot_note: Gujarati one-pot: spiced toor dal with wheat flour dumplings cooked inside.

items.name: Sabudana Khichdi
items._note: Sago/tapioca pearls stir-fried with peanuts and spices. Common Maharashtrian fasting and everyday breakfast.

items.name: Dal Baati Churma
items._one_pot_note: Rajasthani one-pot: baked wheat balls (baati) served with panchmel dal. Churma (sweet) as accompaniment. Fills grain and liquid slots.

items.name: Panchmel Dal
items._note: Five-lentil dal — toor, chana, moong, masoor, urad cooked together. Rajasthani staple, served with dal baati.

items.name: Kadhi
items.meal_note: Curd-based — no separate side needed when kadhi is on the plate.

items.name: Gujarati Kadhi
items._note: Sweeter and thinner than Punjabi/UP kadhi.

items.name: Amti
items._note: Maharashtrian toor dal with tamarind or kokum. Thinner and tangier than North Indian dal.

items.name: Varan
items._note: Plain toor dal, Maharashtrian style. Base of varan-bhaat.

items.name: Pappu
items._note: Andhra toor dal with tamarind — tangier and spicier than generic dal.

items.name: Cholar Dal
items._note: Bengali chana dal with coconut and ghee.

items.name: Moru Kuzhambu
items._note: Yogurt-based curry. Replaces dal in South Indian meals.

items.name: Pulusu (Andhra Tamarind Gravy)
items._note: Thin tamarind-based Andhra gravy. Most common as fish pulusu (chepa pulusu) or prawn pulusu. Sits between rasam and curry in consistency — classified as liquid.

items.name: Kolambu
items._note: Tamarind-based thick liquid — denser than rasam, thinner than curry. Tamil and Andhra staple. Veg version with vegetables; nonveg version (chicken/fish kolambu) uses same base.

items.name: Machher Jhol
items._note: Light Bengali fish curry with potatoes and tomato.

items.name: Shorshe Maach
items._note: Fish in mustard paste — signature Bengali dish.

items.name: Gutti Vankaya
items._note: Stuffed baby brinjal in Andhra spice paste.

items.name: Misal
items._note: Sprouted moth beans in spicy gravy.

items.name: Gongura Chicken
items._note: Chicken cooked with gongura (sorrel) leaves — the defining Andhra nonveg curry. Tangy and spicy.

items.name: Chettinad Fish Curry
items._note: Fish curry in Chettinad spice base — kalpasi, marathi mokku, stone flower. Distinct from generic fish curry.

items.name: Kadala Curry
items._note: Black chickpeas in coconut-spice gravy. Classic Kerala breakfast curry, served with puttu or appam.

items.name: Fish Molee
items._note: Very mild white coconut milk fish curry. Distinct from spicy Malabar-style fish_curry_coconut — no whole spices, no chilli heat.

items.name: Gatte ki Sabzi
items._note: Gram flour dumplings cooked in spiced yogurt curry. Rajasthani staple.

items.name: Egg Curry
items._note: Available to both eggitarian (person_2) and nonveg (person_1) persons.

items.name: Pan Fried Chicken
items.meal_note: As snack: serve with 1 roti + garlic curd dip (~350 kcal, ~30g protein total).

items.name: Ker Sangri
items._note: Dried desert beans (ker) and dried berries (sangri) stir-fried with spices. Quintessential Rajasthani dry sabzi.

items.name: Poriyal
items._note: South Indian dry vegetable stir-fry with mustard seeds and grated coconut. Specific vegetable varies.

items.name: Thoran
items._note: Kerala stir-fry with grated coconut. Lighter and drier than poriyal.

items.name: Kootu
items._note: Semi-dry lentil + vegetable with coconut. Thicker than sambhar, drier than curry.

items.name: Avial
items._note: Mixed vegetables in coconut-yogurt paste.

items.name: Aloo Posto
items._note: Potatoes in poppy seed paste. Quintessential Bengali home dish.

items.name: Chorchori
items._note: Bengali mixed vegetable stir-fry with panch phoron.

items.name: Zunka
items._note: Maharashtrian dry curry made from besan with spices.

items.name: Undhiyu
items._note: Gujarati mixed vegetable, slow-cooked with methi muthiya.

items.name: Batata Bhaji
items._note: Maharashtrian dry spiced potato bhaji. Simpler and drier than aloo jeera — uses mustard seeds and curry leaves.

items.name: Royyala Iguru
items._note: Andhra dry prawn/shrimp masala — thick dry masala clinging to prawns, almost no gravy.

items.name: Koshimbir
items._note: Maharashtrian fresh salad — grated cucumber/carrot with roasted peanuts, grated coconut, lemon, and green chilli. Different from kheera pyaaz salad.

items.name: Kheera Pyaaz Salad
items._note: Standard salad — cucumber, onion, tomato, lemon. Not swappable in v1, always present at lunch and dinner.

items.name: Pesarattu
items._note: Green moong dal crepe, Andhra breakfast.

macro_template._note: All macro fields optional and nullable. Add manually per dish for calorie/protein estimates on home screen (D-13). Display only in v1.
